page_placements.theme: Jailbreak mechanisms: suppressing the refusal direction, direction-guided attacks, and routes outside the single-turn direction

record.file_problem: GitHub repository metadata, README, and file list only; code was not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports a from-scratch reproduction of the mean-difference direction and activation-projection ablation on new instruction-tuned models, with refusal and capability evaluations.
record.gate_note: The README reports results for the direction ablation and related attack/projection evaluations. It also reports results from separate methods such as cipher attacks and many-shot prompting; those are not rows here because they do not test the specified versions. The attack prompt results are recorded where they bear on V3, but first-line refusal classification is distinguished from useful compliance judged by an LLM.
record.test_reason: From-scratch reproduction of the paper's difference-in-means direction and inference-time projection ablation on Qwen2.5, Mistral and Llama-3.1, with the same AdvBench and Alpaca data and substring refusal metric, plus an MMLU capability check. Extensions measure the direction's projection under prompt attacks, with judge-scored compliance, which bears on V3.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The author concludes the single-direction ablation claim survives on all three families, but the 'surgical' framing holds only with a KL-aware (joint) selection criterion; the refusal-only criterion costs 6.0 pp MMLU on Qwen and 3.8 pp on Llama. Prompt attacks lower the direction's projection, mainly through repeated query content, and evade the substring classifier, but give no useful compliance. The direction is therefore not the only mechanism mediating refusal.
record.recipe_differences: From-scratch reproduction of the difference-in-means direction and activation projection, with a layer/position sweep and held-out refusal-rate selection. Adds a joint harmless-KL selection criterion; the README says the paper's Sec. 5 orthogonalization tricks are not implemented. Repository type: replication.
record.method_sensitivity: Selected layer and prompt-token position vary across models. The capability effect varies by model and by refusal-only versus joint min-KL selection. The README reports that generation is capped at 16 tokens and the refusal classifier examines only the first completion line.

fits_no_version.finding: Attacks that lower the refusal-direction projection and first-line refusal leave useful compliance at noise level; the author concludes the direction is not the only refusal mechanism. On Llama, attacks leave 54–81% first-line refusal.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A drop in projection on the single refusal direction, without ablation, is not sufficient for useful harmful compliance; other refusal pathways remain.

record.problems: Repository contents were not independently run or checked. The refusal evaluation uses a first-line substring classifier, 16-token generation cap, and held-out set of 64 AdvBench prompts; the README itself says this classifier overcounts useful compliance. The added judge is Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, and reported uncertainty estimates are not stated. The MMLU check covers five subjects and 1386 questions.
record.rows_left_out: Within the 60-row limit, omitted the additional per-template projection-ranking results and the controlled turn-mechanism tables, as well as separate response-score means, calibration cells, cipher-attack and many-shot results. These appear in the README sections on probe_templates, turn_mechanism, judge calibration/quality, many-shot jailbreaking, and cipher/encoding attacks. They were lower priority than the direct ablation results, reported MMLU subject results, and attack-condition refusal/useful-compliance comparisons.

untested.parts: Inducing refusal by adding the direction to harmless prompts; generation quality beyond 16 tokens; capability on benchmarks other than five MMLU subjects.
Training against direction ablation for robustness; any causal test (e.g., ablating or restoring the direction under attack) that attack effects run through the direction.

missing.what: Number of (layer, position) candidates that drove val refusal to 0 (Qwen 19/85, Mistral 23/100), and the ~80× spread in harmless KL (0.04–3.25 nats) among candidates
missing.locator: README, Refusal-rate ablation; Capability tradeoff (joint-criterion selection)

missing.what: Single-turn template projection ranking on Qwen 7B (vanilla +25.15 to code_comment +13.46, a 47% drop)
Turn-mechanism projection tables (A, B, D, E) for Qwen and Llama, e.g. a same-query prior turn cuts projection from +15.47 to +5.62
Judge calibration on harmless Alpaca (UC 83.3% Qwen, 91.7% Mistral), needed to interpret the UC rows

record.verdict_notes: The source is a README only. The repo is unreviewed, n=64 test prompts, no uncertainty reported, 16-token generation cap, first-line substring classifier. V2 is not tested: the repo uses inference-time projection, not a weight edit. The 'additional refusal pathways' remark for Llama is author speculation, not a V4 test. Cipher and many-shot results do not involve the direction and are correctly excluded. The V3 first-line refusal rows are kept as cannot_determine because they lack paired projections.

versions.untested_parts: Tests removal and MMLU capability retention. Does not test adding the direction to induce refusals on harmless requests.
No weight-edit or released-model abliteration result is reported; this repo uses inference-time activation projection.

Tests prompt conditions alongside refusal-direction projections and behavioral evaluations. Does not test training against direction ablation for robustness, or establish causally that the prompt effects operate through the direction.
No direct test of affine, cone, or multiple-direction geometry, or a causal test of other refusal directions.
Does not separately measure harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.
No cross-language, base-to-instruct, or other stated transfer test.
No controlled comparison of refusal-training procedures or stages.

relation.reason: The study's own refusal-ablation and MMLU results bear directly on V1. Its attack projection and judge results bear on V3.

tranche.reason: A from-scratch reproduction of the difference-in-means direction with projection at every block output. It uses held-out refusal-rate selection and a substring refusal metric, as in Arditi. The V3 extensions are extra, new-setting work.

source_check.notes: Every result is a single run with no uncertainty: 64 test prompts, 32 val, a 16-token cap and a first-line substring classifier. The README text does not say Arditi's selection used a KL filter. Other pack statements say it had one (<0.1), so refusal-only is a simplified criterion. Attack projections come only from Qwen and Llama.
